VBO:0008086.summary: A working pursuit hound, the Turkish Greyhound is kept for hunting quail, partridge, rabbits and foxes in central and southern Anatolia. Locally called Tazi, it is especially associated with Konya and Şanlıurfa, including wetland hunting grounds. Smaller local populations have also been documented from Kars and Iğdır to Ankara and Istanbul.
VBO:0008086.shortDescription: A Turkish pursuit hound with a varied hunting repertoire, rooted especially in Konya and Şanlıurfa’s local Tazi populations.

sources.title: Yilmaz, Ertugrul and Wilson: Turkey’s native guard and hunting dogs (2012)
sources.evidence: Actual pp8–9: Turkish Tazi concentrated in Konya and Sanliurfa, smaller populations in Igdir/Kars/Karaman/Ankara/Istanbul. Own2011 fieldwork cited for use hunting quail, partridge, rabbits and foxes mainly in central/southern Anatolian wetlands. Actual Figure7 caption identifies Turkish Tazi in prime condition without/with rug, photographs credited Orhan Yilmaz. Body paragraph specifies long limbs, slim body, thin bare tail, long slender skull/neck, deep chest, flexible curved spine and variable short coat colors. Pooled numerical means not imposed on an adult. Claimed ancient Taigan descent, generic Saluki comparison,65km/h, mild/loyal/child/cat claims with popular-book sourcing excluded.
